title: The Cost of Unclear Leadership
author: Summer Mulder
summary: Unclear leadership erodes organizations quietly but expensively. Mulder identifies the core problem: leaders who know what they want but fear the discomfort of enforcing it. When standards aren't enforced, resistance gets rewarded, wrong performers gain power, accountability disappears, and good people underperform due to exhaustion and guessing. Clarity is not harsh or controlling but respect for the mission and team, and leaders who enforce clear standards see everything around them rise.
points: Unclear leadership stems from fear of discomfort, not lack of vision or direction.
Unenforced standards teach teams that rules are optional and reward resistance.
Lack of clarity costs money through rework, delays, miscommunications, and turnover.
Clarity is respect: for the work, the mission, the team, and yourself.
Start with one standard, state it clearly, enforce it gently, hold it consistently.
quotes: I knew exactly what I wanted. I just didn't want to deal with the discomfort of enforcing it.
When a leader lets things slide, the whole culture slides with it.
Nothing is more frustrating than trying to hit a target you can't see.

The leader who avoids clarity always pays the highest price, usually quietly, and usually alone. But the leader who enforces clarity? Everything around them rises. Standards rise. Communication rises. Performance rises. Trust rises.” Archived from Summer Mulder Substack on April 20, 2026 by Tim.
